nationalSpirits.description: The Bureau of Ordnance influences any ship designs made.  This spirit is available due to our amazing torpedoes.
nationalSpirits.name: Bureau of Ordnance

nationalSpirits.description: Afghanistan is a land defined by its large tribal population, with many of its people effectively ruling themselves with little input from the capital. Afghanistan is however a land also defined by significant ethnic division and religious traditionalism, with intertribal conflicts and Pashtun chauvinism being common place. These divides have long frustrated Amanullah's attempts at modernisation, although this tribal autonomy has had the silver lining of many simply not caring about what happens in [267.Controller.GetVictoryPointName_12769], much to the King's benefit.
nationalSpirits.name: Land of Villages, Tribes, and Faiths

nationalSpirits.description: In the early months of 1929, troops loyal to King Amanullah saw off the largest rebellion to his rule so far, led by the bandit king Habibullāh Kalakāni and his band of Saqqawists. Supported by much of the traditionalist Ulema and Kalakāni's fellow Tajiks, they had aimed to overthrow Amanullah and reverse his years of modernisation. While Kalakāni may have perished, the escape of many of his loyalists to Bukhara, led by his uncle Purdil Khan, has long been one of the sharpest thorns in the regime's side. Even with their defeat, fears about the exiled movement's growing strength across the border has many convinced that a second rebellion is inevitable.
nationalSpirits.name: Spectre of Rebellion

nationalSpirits.description: The Fourth Anglo-Afghan War of 1926, or to those in India the \"Afghan Occupation of the Frontier\", has long been a source of pride for the Afghan nation. While Afghanistan's freedom was won in the third war just a few years prior, the failure to secure the region now commonly referred to as Pashtunistan weighted heavily on its people. Its capture following rebellions during the Raj's collapse wiped away this shame, and even when people begin to question the government they remember what has been won for them.  For those in Pashtunistan however, their integration into Afghanistan has been a bittersweet one, with the frontier operating more as an independent nation in its own right rather than part of a single whole. Many who once cheered as they saw Afghan troops ride across the border now see their ties to [267.Controller.GetVictoryPointName_12769] as little more than a weight holding them down, believing they would be better off fully independent or integrated into India.
nationalSpirits.name: Loy Afghanistan

nationalSpirits.description: Despite significant developments towards the end of the last decade, especially in response to the Fourth Anglo-Afghan War and major rebellions against the crown that defined those years, the Royal Afghan Army has slowly begun to stagnate. Funding meant for the armed forces has in recent years found its way instead into Amanullah's own pet projects, a bigger focus now for the King, something that has drawn significant ire from its leadership. The silver lining for them however is that over recent months the king has slowly seemed more and more receptive of their demands for army reform, and expect it to begin full scale going into the new year.
nationalSpirits.name: Stagnant Army

nationalSpirits.description: Even after years of reforms and modernisation efforts, Afghanistan finds itself a heavily decentralised backwater. While attempts to further centralise and develop the nation will inevitably lead to conflict, it is believed by the country's reformers that these growing pains must be tolerated for Afghanistan to rise again as the great power it deserves to be.
nationalSpirits.name: National Integration

nationalSpirits.description: With the establishment of an independent Albania, two parties in Albania have managed to take power: the social-democratic Unity Party led by Avni Rustemi and the conservative Progressive Party led by Shefqet Vërlaci. With the two parties having differing goals, yet both having vast influence, it's no wonder that, in recent years, Albania has become such a politically polarised nation...
nationalSpirits.name: Polarised Nation

nationalSpirits.description: Education in Albania is very poor, with eighty per cent of the population illiterate. In addition, education is neither compulsory nor does Albania have any formal university. The only group of people within our nation to possess some sort of education are the aristocrats, meaning that we are severely behind our European counterparts when it comes to research and are viewed as a backwater. Separate Turkish schools for Muslims and Greek schools for Orthodox Christians have not helped this issue one bit.
nationalSpirits.name: Mass Illiteracy

nationalSpirits.description: The Anti-Concessions Movement and general hostility toward the former establishment has roused a groundswell of support for the Anqing Clique. China deserves to be free of German imperialism, and the people's support is proof!
nationalSpirits.name: Righteous Cause

nationalSpirits.description: Popular support for our cause is large, and as a result, many are begging to join the ranks of our army to finally free ourselves of the German chains.
nationalSpirits.name: Anti-Concessionist Militias

nationalSpirits.description: Despite various claims, there has never really been a \"Chinese Army\". Instead, the military is decentralised, highly factional, and irregular - the armies of the various warlords and breakaway states having grown haphazardly and semi-independently over decades of conflict. Most significant forces are regional, oversized, poorly maintained, and distrustful of one another, if not outright hostile. Corruption is endemic. Where logistics exist, most are simple coolie or mule trains complemented by regular robbery of the surrounding countryside. Though a few units appear to meet western standards, the vast majority do not, and better resemble gangs of bandits and other criminals. Even in peacetime, mere word of an approaching army is often enough for local peasants to flee the oncoming wave of looting and abuse.

effects.label: Supply Combat Penalties on Core Territory

nationalSpirits.name: Warlord Era Inadequacies

nationalSpirits.description: With the old League of Eight Provinces in ruin and anti-concessionist rhetoric running rampant, Chen Tiaoyuan has successfully pushed himself forward as a beacon for the movement in China. Those that enabled his rise however could just as easily let him fall should he betray their interests. Nonetheless, Chen Tiaoyuan knows very well that following their every wish will lead to an Anqing without the resources necessary to bring about this liberation of China.
nationalSpirits.name: Credibility of Chen Tiaoyuan

nationalSpirits.description: The Bureau of Ordnance influences any ship designs made.  This spirit is available due to our amazing torpedoes.
nationalSpirits.name: Bureau of Ordnance

nationalSpirits.description: Following the coup, many in Argentina were concerned about future purges and breaches of people's rights by the new regime. Their concerns have not come true since Carlés maintains his influence on the government and society restricted, and the populace in return does not oppose the new administration strongly.
nationalSpirits.name: Political Control Over Argentina

nationalSpirits.description: Letting either side of the Armed Forces get too much influence has severe consequences and could even lead to a military coup
nationalSpirits.name: Interservice Rivalry - Navy Dominant

nationalSpirits.description: For centuries now, hundreds of thousands of Armenians have seen themselves forced to migrate to faraway places, and are now living scattered across Europe, the Americas, and the Middle East. Ever since the start of our revolt against the Ottoman Empire, an increasing number of them has begun the journey back to the homeland of their ancestors. However, many are still being held back by their fear of the Ottomans subjugating our nation once again.
nationalSpirits.name: Return of the Armenian Diaspora

nationalSpirits.description: In the chaotic aftermath of Britain's downfall, many ships fled to Australasia to find refuge - far more than could be maintained in the country's meagre ports. Even with many ships mothballed, it still is too much for Australia to handle. A solution needs to be found.
nationalSpirits.name: Oversized Fleet

nationalSpirits.description: Australasia's economy was never particularly strong, and the aftermath of the Weltkrieg has only made it much, much worse. Opportunity is not present, and people cannot find jobs. Radicalisation is beginning to take root across the country as more extreme solutions begin to be considered.
nationalSpirits.name: Economic Depression

nationalSpirits.description: We gave everything we had in the Weltkrieg and then some, and it shows. Nearly everybody knew someone who died far from home for a war that meant nothing in the end and have no desire to see such a thing happen again, not unless it is absolutely necessary.
nationalSpirits.name: Bled Dry

nationalSpirits.description: During the Weltkrieg, the Australian and New Zealanders were the most aggressive, and managed to keep their form in spite of their questionable discipline. Out of the line they were undoubtedly difficult to handle, but once in it they loved a fight. They were a curious mixture of toughness and sentimentality.
nationalSpirits.name: ANZAC Spirit

nationalSpirits.description: A population of agrarian and tribal descent, one of the main issues plaguing the Basra project is the lack of skilled personnel as forced and voluntary exclusion from the Ottoman educational system has greatly hampered the capabilities of our people. Whilst there is no lack of Assyrians with a clerical education, we severely lack engineers, scientists and educators.
nationalSpirits.name: Technical Illiteracy

nationalSpirits.description: An unfair and theocratic land system has only accentuated the crippling poverty that has come to represent the Assyrians in Basra. Forced to live in shanty towns, struggling settlements in the marshes of the Lower Euphrates or in the shadow of their richer Muslim and Jewish neighbours, the war for independence has given rise to calls for a redistribution of wealth. Great differences in wealth and status between the Arabic Christians, integrated in the Ottoman system, and the adherents of the Assyrian Church of the East only further complicate the issue and have brought division into an already struggling community.
nationalSpirits.name: Crippling Poverty

nationalSpirits.description: Venerated as a Saint by his people, the patriarch of the Assyrian Church of the East has developed a union of church and state over the years wherein he and his inner circle, mostly consisting of family members, have governed and represented the Assyrian people as kings. This situation, of which Mar Shimun has grown rather fond has obstructed other political formations and given rise to a sizeable anti-patriarchal front that desires equal representation.
nationalSpirits.name: Patriarchal Dictatorship

nationalSpirits.description: The lower Mesopotamian plain has for centuries been the home of the Arab Shiites and various small splinter movements of the Abrahamic faiths. The arrival of the Assyrians in this previously Muslim dominated land has greatly upset the balance of power and their push for a Christian state in the Levant has excluded large portions of the native population. The Muslim population, desiring unification with Baghdad and their religious freedom guaranteed has become a thorn in the side of the Assyrian government as their protests, obstructionism and even guerrilla warfare in the marshes of Lower Mesopotamia continue to harass our goals.
nationalSpirits.name: Ethnic-Religious Divide

nationalSpirits.description: Chaldeans, Nestorians, Protestants and Catholics. The Assyrian community, lacking strong religious authority and unity has splintered over the years and given rise to a plethora of separate communities, further amplified by missionary work of the French, Americans and British during the 19th century. With Mar Shimun of the Assyrian Church of the East harbouring the desire to crown himself king and the other groups feeling underrepresented in the new Assyrian administration, Assyria has its work carved out.
nationalSpirits.name: Assyrian Division

nationalSpirits.description: The Crown of Hungary refuses to pay their taxes into the common coffers for the common ministries.  They are still discontent with the formation of the Kingdom of Illyria as a resolution of the South Slavic revolts of 1926, and see themselves as betrayed by the Viennese government. They wish to be compensated for the loss of the Croatian lands.
nationalSpirits.name: Austro-Hungarian Ties Broken

nationalSpirits.description: The Vienna Circle is a group of philosophers and scientists, drawn from the natural and social sciences, logic and mathematics, who have met regularly at the University of Vienna since 1924.  The central thought behind their activities was "Exact Thinking on the Edge of Doom".
nationalSpirits.name: The Vienna Circle

nationalSpirits.description: Officially titled the Central European Economic Union, Mitteleuropa is a customs and economic union unifying Germany and its sphere of influence, established after the Weltkrieg. Member states of Mitteleuropa find the impact of this agreement mixed - while the economic connections with Germany are beneficial, the agreement is heavily weighted in German favour.
nationalSpirits.name: Member of Mitteleuropa

nationalSpirits.description: With the Legation Cities' enhanced focus on free trade to all parties, said all parties are benefiting handsomely.
nationalSpirits.name: Fruits of the Open Door

nationalSpirits.description: Officially titled the Central European Economic Union, Mitteleuropa is a customs and economic union unifying Germany and its sphere of influence, established after the Weltkrieg. Member states of Mitteleuropa find the impact of this agreement mixed - while the economic connections with Germany are beneficial, the agreement is heavily weighted in German favour.
nationalSpirits.name: Member of Mitteleuropa

nationalSpirits.description: The political system of the United Baltic Duchy is based upon centuries of tradition, stemming from the Livonian Confederation or, in some cases, even earlier. The system of semi-direct representation through Landtags, an enduring loyalty to Provincial Ostsee Civil Law, and the autonomous nature of the Baltic Knighthoods, are all undoubtedly a part of the Baltic German identity - and yet, it is a system in dire need of reform.
nationalSpirits.name: Byzantine Political System

nationalSpirits.description: The Baltic Territorial Army is the volunteer defence force of the United Baltic Duchy, formed in 1918 under the guidance of German commander Rüdiger von der Goltz. It is ethnically segregated between Baltic German, Latvian, Estonian and Russian units, and unpopular with the native majority population. This has pressed the Landeswehr to reform and modernise to make up for its manpower shortages. Largely independent of civilian oversight, and for good reason, it is efficient and innovative, considered to be the most elite force in the Reichspakt.
nationalSpirits.name: The Baltische Landeswehr

nationalSpirits.description: All citizens of the United Baltic Duchy are able to move to and work in the German Empire without inhibition, and vice versa. Two decades ago, it was believed that this would foster German colonisation of the Baltic states via immigrants from the Heimat. It has had the opposite result, however - young Baltic Germans move to Berlin, Saxony and the Ruhr in search of a living, abandoning their family homes.
nationalSpirits.name: Emigration

nationalSpirits.description: Officially titled the Central European Economic Union, Mitteleuropa is a customs and economic union unifying Germany and its sphere of influence, established after the Weltkrieg. Member states of Mitteleuropa find the impact of this agreement mixed - while the economic connections with Germany are beneficial, the agreement is heavily weighted in German favour.
nationalSpirits.name: Member of Mitteleuropa

nationalSpirits.description: After the Weltkrieg ended in crushing defeat for our small nation, King Albert I was forced into exile and has followed the British Royal Family to Canada. Adored by all of his citizens for his bravery during the Weltkrieg, earning him the nickname 'Soldier King', large royalist underground movements plot his return to the throne and an end to German occupation.
nationalSpirits.name: King Albert I in Exile

nationalSpirits.description: While the majority of the population lives in Dutch speaking Flanders, French speaking Wallonia held the upper hand during most of the 19th century until the Weltkrieg. While the situation was abruptly reversed by the German occupier due to their 'Flamenpolitik', this has only increased tensions between the two groups causing a divide that has proven hard to heal. The army in particular is heavily affected by this with Walloon soldiers not understanding their Flemish superiors or refusing to do so.
nationalSpirits.name: Linguistic Debacle

nationalSpirits.description: High tax rates, favouritism towards Germans and a general lack of interest by German administrators and industrialists in Flemish-Walloon living conditions have only worsened the aversion for the German Regime causing large social inequality and unrest, especially in Wallonia.
nationalSpirits.name: Anti-German Sentiment

nationalSpirits.description: Officially titled the Central European Economic Union, Mitteleuropa is a customs and economic union unifying Germany and its sphere of influence, established after the Weltkrieg. Member states of Mitteleuropa find the impact of this agreement mixed - while the economic connections with Germany are beneficial, the agreement is heavily weighted in German favour.
nationalSpirits.name: Member of Mitteleuropa

nationalSpirits.description: With the Legation Cities' enhanced focus on free trade to all parties, said all parties are benefiting handsomely.
nationalSpirits.name: Fruits of the Open Door

nationalSpirits.description: Bhutan is a political time capsule, with a backwards society straight out of medieval times. Serfs labour throughout the year to collect enough food to survive, and little industry exists outside of the cottage workshops of wealthy lords and small tradeposts. The armed forces of the kingdom rely on the banners of penlops, who gather together bands of warriors from their domains. There is a place in the Himalayas where time has stood still, and Bhutan has been left behind by the world at large.
nationalSpirits.name: The Hermit Kingdom

nationalSpirits.description: Much of Bhutan is comprised of semi-independent monastic fiefdoms, making them one of the most powerful forces in the kingdom.
nationalSpirits.name: Monastic Control

nationalSpirits.description: Our nation is governed by a patchwork of Penlops and smaller lordlings, who divide their time between furthering their personal interests and those of the state. Much of the nation is managed by monasteries and feudal lords and our government is forced to cooperate with them to action government policy and manage the realm.
nationalSpirits.name: Precarious Central Authority

nationalSpirits.description: Ever since Ugyen Wangchuck united the penlops under his iron fist more than three decades ago, the once squabbling lands of the mountain kingdom have been wrangled into sleepy peace. With so little happening this far up in the Himalayas, most have stopped bothering to worry over military matters.
nationalSpirits.name: Peace in our Time

nationalSpirits.description: The majority of the White Ruthenian population consists of illiterate peasants. Since gaining independence, the country has invested significant resources to create and improve a national education system. This multi-generational task is only starting to bring results, slowly improving life in the countryside.
nationalSpirits.name: Mass Illiteracy

nationalSpirits.description: When White Ruthenia was fighting for its independence and national revival, the largely socialist Sojm initially outlawed private ownership of land and called for the redistribution of all large estates without compensation to landowners, largely ethnic Poles. However, this policy was quickly tempered as the Sojm sought support from the German Empire and the Belarusian Social-Democratic Party distanced themselves further from Bolshevik Russia. As such, more moderate land redistribution, which included compensation to landlords, has been in place since 1921. However, the slow pace and numerous problems encountered led to criticism within the BSDP and from its leftist coalition partners, calling for a radical policy to replace it as the Belarusian Socialist Hramada had promised back in 1917.
nationalSpirits.name: Agrarian Society

nationalSpirits.description: While many nations in Eastern Europe have experienced a national awakening in the second half of the 19th century, the idea of a Belarusian nation only started to appear in the early 20th century. By the time Russia fell to the Bolsheviks, very few Belarusians could even comprehend the idea of nationalism, let alone embrace it, and many even considered Belarusians to be nothing but Polonised Russians or poor, uncultured peasants unworthy of the title of \"nation\". Since 1917, Belarusian intellectuals have been fighting an uphill battle to bring education and, through it, national identity to the poor, illiterate peasants of the region. Even now, the majority of the population is apathetic at best or hostile at worst to the idea of Belarusian nationhood.
nationalSpirits.name: Weak National Identity

nationalSpirits.description: Officially titled the Central European Economic Union, Mitteleuropa is a customs and economic union unifying Germany and its sphere of influence, established after the Weltkrieg. Member states of Mitteleuropa find the impact of this agreement mixed - while the economic connections with Germany are beneficial, the agreement is heavily weighted in German favour.
nationalSpirits.name: Member of Mitteleuropa

nationalSpirits.description: Tensions rise as vastly different factions prepare for what will probably be the most violent and contentious election in the history of Brazil. Political talk is almost synonymous with heated arguments, and an air of ideological extremism looms over the nation's populace.
nationalSpirits.name: Election Year Tensions

nationalSpirits.description: The United States of Brazil has always prized the autonomy of its states. Each has its own president, its own political parties, and its own military, and the people have shown themselves willing to die for these regional rights. However, this does result in a very weak and toothless central government, which cannot act decisively when required.
nationalSpirits.name: Extreme Decentralisation

nationalSpirits.description: Few wounds take longer to heal than a civil war. The War Between the States left thousands dead, and many more orphaned and homeless, as the tensions between the political oligarchies and regional identities finally boiled over to the battlefield after troops from Minas Gerais trespassed into São Paulo. Any actions the central government tries to do are now viewed with immense distrust, and the sheer damage caused on the border between Rio and São Paulo has not yet been fully been repaired.
nationalSpirits.name: Wake of the War

nationalSpirits.description: Brazil's armed forces are, simply put, a ragtag group of 26 state militias, a so called 'Federal Army' in Rio de Janeiro, and its navy is pretty much the only arm of the military under actual federal chafing. These archaically organised forces have immensely differing quality in both training and equipment, and are simply unsuited to modern combat in any way whatsoever, especially if required to fight for a nation they feel little allegiance to.
nationalSpirits.name: Divided Military

nationalSpirits.description: Our society is traditionally quite nomadic, consisting in large part of wandering tribes migrating alongside their herds of livestock. The rise of railroads has revived many of the old cities and created new ones, though the recent settlement of foreigners has done much to disrupt our way of life. We will have to face facts, however, that the age of the nomad is coming to a close, and if we want to compete on the world stage we will have to adapt to the new industrial age.
nationalSpirits.name: Land of Wanderers

nationalSpirits.description: There are distinct tensions between the many branches of the Emirate's government. In recent years, the well-oiled machinery of the state has ground to a halt, as Emir Alim Khan has begun favouring intervening more directly in the affairs of his ministers. Fearful of the Jadid dominated Majlis, the Emir has left the central organ of government leaderless, instead filling postings with yes-men and loyalists. There is a fear amongst the reformists that the state bureaucracy is close to breaking down completely, whilst the conservatives criticize the current administrative system as having been hollowed out and ruined by reformists.
nationalSpirits.name: Struggling Bureaucracy

nationalSpirits.description: Although Emir Alim Khan personally studied at Russian military academies and has long been aided by Russian advisors, our attempts to reform the Bukharian army is a continuous struggle with few happy results. Most of our fighting force is still a glorified levy and tribal militia, to be called on in times of crisis. The standing army is showing promise, but has been slow to adapt to modern equipment and new tactics. Something must be done, before we are thrust into another war.
nationalSpirits.name: Antiquated Army

nationalSpirits.description: At the height of the Central Asian insurrection, the Russian Republic recognized us as an independent state with dominion over the region of Samarkand. Regardless of this new geopolitical arrangement, our old hegemon still projects a great deal of influence over our economy. Russian capital and machinery have brought great technological and economic advancement to Bukhara. Almost all of the earnings from these new railways, cotton plantations, and gold mines go to their Russian owners, however, leaving us with only a paltry share of profits that were generated from our nation's fertile land and plentiful resources.
nationalSpirits.name: Russian Economic Control

nationalSpirits.description: Twenty years after the Weltkrieg, faith in the ideal of \"Greater Bulgaria\" is fading. Shackled by internal division and ethnic conflict, Bulgaria has spent the past two decades going from crisis to crisis, and has withdrawn to internal affairs. An impressionable observer might still think that Bulgaria is a Balkan hegemon, but in reality, its power to dominate has long since waned.
nationalSpirits.name: Waning Hegemony

nationalSpirits.description: Founded not long after the Weltkrieg, the Military League is the organisation unifying Bulgaria's massive war veteran corps and representing the interests of the military in civilian affairs. Manifesting their political power in organisations such as Zveno, the Military League holds unprecedented power in the country and represents an unspoken threat to democracy.
nationalSpirits.name: Military League

nationalSpirits.description: Crown Prince Boris, the eldest son of Ferdinand, is a savvy, clever and popular figure, granting confidence to the people that the next monarch will be just as capable. He always reaches out to the people, he often drives by car across the country with no guards, stopping to converse with peasants, workers and children - there isn't a village in Bulgaria that does not have a person who hasn't ridden with the Crown Prince.
nationalSpirits.name: Prince of the People

nationalSpirits.description: Passed during the authoritarian rule of Konstantin Georgiev, the State Protection Act gives the government authoritarian powers in uprooting opposition and dissidents. For now, it has managed to maintain order in Bulgaria, but it grows more and more controversial by the day.  Democracy in Bulgaria lives or dies with the future of this bill.
nationalSpirits.name: State Protection Act

nationalSpirits.description: Officially titled the Central European Economic Union, Mitteleuropa is a customs and economic union unifying Germany and its sphere of influence, established after the Weltkrieg. Member states of Mitteleuropa find the impact of this agreement mixed - while the economic connections with Germany are beneficial, the agreement is heavily weighted in German favour.
nationalSpirits.name: Member of Mitteleuropa

nationalSpirits.description: The Kuomintang may have democratic and populist ideals, but it has a long way to go in terms of making those ideals into a reality. For the peasants and workers of China, plenty of dreamers have come and gone with their utopian promises and few have delivered. Battlefield victories may prove Kuomintang tenacity and perhaps may unify China under its banner, but if they wish to truly win over the hearts of the people, they must first save the hard-pressed commoners from their perennial strife.  It will take a long period of state building and careful policy implementation for the common people to see the Nationalist Government as legitimate, haughty declarations and fancy parades aside. In the meantime, plenty see the Kuomintang as hardly a step up from the warlord strongmen or as dangerous stooges of the faraway Syndicalist powers.
nationalSpirits.name: Legitimacy of the Party: Abysmal

nationalSpirits.description: For almost a decade since the failure of the Northern Expedition, the National Revolutionary Army of the Chinese Kuomintang was reduced to a shadow of its former self. Those that believed that the revolution could still be fought for fled for the hills of Fujian where they have engaged in a guerrilla insurgency for the past years, launching a brave but failed uprising in 1932. Despite their prior failures, the NRA continues to fight, maintaining an asymmetrical war against League authorities.
nationalSpirits.name: Insurgency of the NRA

Instead, the military is decentralised, highly factional, and irregular - the armies of the various warlords and breakaway states having grown haphazardly and semi-independently over decades of conflict. Most significant forces are regional, oversized, poorly maintained, and distrustful of one another, if not outright hostile. Corruption is endemic. Where logistics exist, most are simple coolie or mule trains complemented by regular robbery of the surrounding countryside. Though a few units appear to meet western standards, the vast majority do not, and better resemble gangs of bandits and other criminals. Even in peacetime, mere word of an approaching army is often enough for local peasants to flee the oncoming wave of looting and abuse.

nationalSpirits.name: Warlord Era Inadequacies

nationalSpirits.description: Ever since the original revolution in 1931, Santiago remains the centre of syndicalism in South America. Many of the people are willing to die defending their ideology against the reactionaries that surround us.
nationalSpirits.name: Home of South American Syndicalism

nationalSpirits.description: The Monroe Doctrine enacted by the US has caused our nation to lack a significant military force or the ability to go to war with other American countries in general. While this ensures the safety of our country, it severely limits the idea of expansion.

effects.label: Justify war goal time on us

nationalSpirits.name: Monroe Doctrine

nationalSpirits.description: Strong traditions of democracy and progressive reforms over the last few decades have led to Costa Rica being seen abroad as the shining beacon of Central American democracy.
nationalSpirits.name: Beacon of Democracy

nationalSpirits.description: The United Fruit Company holds vast power in our nation's economy and has deep ties within the government. While the lingering American Depression has proven detrimental to their influence abroad, making way for increasing German trade, the company and its terrible labour practices have led to rising tensions in the political landscape. With elections just around the corner and socialism entrenching itself all around Central America, this could escalate without proper government intervention.
nationalSpirits.name: UFC Labour Conflicts

nationalSpirits.description: The United Fruit Company or the UFC has built railways, infrastructure and housing to expand their operations in our country, but the terrible practices that their employees have to endure has earned them a terrible reputation.
nationalSpirits.name: Influence of the UFC

nationalSpirits.description: The Zentralamerikanische Kaffee-Gesellschaft or ZKG was created by coffee barons of German descent to protect and expand their influence over the Costa Rican government and expand their plantations in the central valley.
nationalSpirits.name: Influence of the ZKG

nationalSpirits.description: The Croatian people fought to make an Illyria free of Austria a reality, while the rest of the so called Illyrians hid in their cities and did nothing. It is for this reason that we must restrict all officer positions to Croatians at the cost of alienating the rest of our countrymen.
nationalSpirits.name: Croatian Officers

nationalSpirits.description: Officially titled the Central European Economic Union, Mitteleuropa is a customs and economic union unifying Germany and its sphere of influence, established after the Weltkrieg. Member states of Mitteleuropa find the impact of this agreement mixed - while the economic connections with Germany are beneficial, the agreement is heavily weighted in German favour.
nationalSpirits.name: Member of Mitteleuropa

nationalSpirits.description: The policies of young President Rafael Trejo and the Unionist party have partially alleviated the effects of the great depression.
nationalSpirits.name: Partial Depression Recovery

nationalSpirits.description: The United States is highly influential in Cuban society and politics, and the Americans closely observe and at times directly cause Cuban political developments. Any substantial change in the status-quo is likely to provoke an American response.
nationalSpirits.name: Pervasive American Influence

nationalSpirits.description: The Cuban military holds a great deal of political power including guaranteed congressional seats and is nearly completely unbeholden to the civilian government.
nationalSpirits.name: Mixed Regime

nationalSpirits.description: We currently lease the significant Guantanamo Bay naval base to [GTM.GetNameWithFlag].  Guantanamo Bay was occupied by the United States during the Cuban War of Independence as part of the larger Spanish-American war. In the years and decades thereafter, American control over Guantanamo Bay under nominal Cuban sovereignty was reaffirmed and the Guantanamo Bay naval base was greatly expanded. Whoever controls Guantanamo Bay, the United States or some other imperial power, will surely reap significant benefit.
nationalSpirits.name: Guantanamo Bay Lease

nationalSpirits.description: Enosis or the unification of Greece and Cyprus has been the centrepoint of Cypriot politics and propaganda for decades. First under the Ottomans, then the British and finally again the Turks, the Greek Orthodox population of the island has been quasi unanimous in their support for the movement.
nationalSpirits.name: Desire for Enosis

nationalSpirits.description: Whilst the Greek population of the Greek Isles does not hide their aversion to the Turkish regime, the situation is substantially different for the Turkish population of these islands. Turkish Cypriots and other Muslim groups spread out over isles such as Rhodos don't share their compatriots desire for a quick union with Greece and would rather continue to live and work within the Ottoman framework than partake in a strictly Christian nation wherein they would be an insignificant minority.
nationalSpirits.name: Divided Loyalties

nationalSpirits.description: Officially titled the Central European Economic Union, Mitteleuropa is a customs and economic union unifying Germany and its sphere of influence, established after the Weltkrieg. Member states of Mitteleuropa find the impact of this agreement mixed - while the economic connections with Germany are beneficial, the agreement is heavily weighted in German favour.
nationalSpirits.name: Member of Mitteleuropa

nationalSpirits.description: Nederlandsch-Indië, is the result of Dutch global prominence in spice and cash crop within South East Asia since the 19th century. Its wealth helps fuel the economy of the Netherlands, to much discontent from the locals.
nationalSpirits.name: Colonial Government

nationalSpirits.description: Years of cutbacks to funding, neglect, and mismanagement have left the KNIL in a sorry state. Further to this, with growing resentment from the natives from the local population, recruitment has proven a challenge.
nationalSpirits.name: KNIL: Deficient

nationalSpirits.description: The Danish upper house is under the control of the opposition, hamstringing the government's capacity to make laws.
nationalSpirits.name: Landsting Controlled by Opposition

nationalSpirits.description: The Danish army and the Danish defence system as a whole are afflicted by a lack of control in military leadership. A significant portion of the budget is initially deliberated in the Rigsdag and is overseen by the Minister of Defence. Recently, the foreign minister, Peter Munch, has continued to impede army developments in his pursuit of ultimately abolishing it. Consequently, while the government has the ability to allocate funds for projects without delay, the army is unable to maintain the optimal level of strength.
nationalSpirits.name: Army in Neglect

nationalSpirits.description: The Danish navy is made up of mainly older destroyers and submarines, and due to Denmark's middling naval budget and naval industry, there is little that can be produced besides screening vessels. Much of the fleet as it stands has been refitted to modern standards, but that does not display much aptitude for new design development. Our flagship, the Peder Skram, is a relic from before the Weltkrieg and is largely obsolete, a sister ship of the Herluf Trolle and Olfert Fischer, which have been sold for scrap amidst the disastrous cost to maintain them. Navy leadership is largely bent to the will of the state budget, which has been diverted towards other economic and social affairs.
nationalSpirits.name: Outdated Navy

nationalSpirits.description: The Pacifist Accord, or the agreement for neutrality, particularly with Radikale Venstre Peter Munch, holds strong with general support from Socialdemokratiet and Radikale Venstre's coalition. The eventual end goal of demolishing the army and pursuing true neutrality at the behest of the coalition hamstrings any efforts for the government to militarise. The opposition and even King Christian X have decried that Denmark must remilitarise, citing the Syndicalist threats in Paris and London, but Socialdemokratiet and Radikale Venstre have been silent on the matter.  The moderate left coalition aims to pass a new demilitarisation bill come 1937, since it was denied several years ago. For now, remilitarisation will have severe costs, and conscription is disabled.
nationalSpirits.name: Pacifist Accord

nationalSpirits.description: Officially titled the Central European Economic Union, Mitteleuropa is a customs and economic union unifying Germany and its sphere of influence, established after the Weltkrieg. Member states of Mitteleuropa find the impact of this agreement mixed - while the economic connections with Germany are beneficial, the agreement is heavily weighted in German favour.
nationalSpirits.name: Member of Mitteleuropa

nationalSpirits.description: The Great Depression, which has so devastated the United States, has been nearly as destructive to the economy of the Dominican Republic, and the incompetence of the nation's past Presidents has served to compound the problem. While the economic situation has at last begun to improve, continued recovery is uncertain.
nationalSpirits.name: Great Depression

nationalSpirits.description: The policies of President Martínez and increasingly populist outlook of all major political organisations, as well as the unchecked influence of the military have all contributed to the growth of resentment among the nation's entrenched upper-classes. While this anger may not pose an immediate political threat, it is extremely harmful.
nationalSpirits.name: Hostile Elite

nationalSpirits.description: The economy of Egypt is rather underdeveloped and largely agrarian in nature. Though some industrialisation has begun, it has yet to truly affect the country. Major reforms are needed to get over this hurdle.
nationalSpirits.name: Agrarian Economy

nationalSpirits.description: The vast majority of Egypt's rural populace is illiterate. In order to rectify this hurdle, a programme of education reform must be undertaken.
nationalSpirits.name: Illiterate Populace

nationalSpirits.description: The Egyptian Officer Corps is rather inexperienced as the British and Ottomans wished to make sure they did not grow too powerful. Many are still used to ways of fighting from before the Weltkrieg which is hampering the army. If we are going to make Egypt a modern country we shall need to do some proper reforms of the army.
nationalSpirits.name: Inexperienced Military

nationalSpirits.description: The vast majority of Egypt's land belongs to land-owning elites and nobles, with less than 6% of Egypt's populace owning over 65 percent of her land. In quite a number of these estates, the conditions are likened to those of the Iqta system of old.
nationalSpirits.name: Land Owning Elites

nationalSpirits.description: The Monroe Doctrine enacted by the US has caused our nation to lack a significant military force or the ability to go to war with other American countries in general. While this ensures the safety of our country, it severely limits the idea of expansion.

effects.label: Justify war goal time on us

nationalSpirits.name: Monroe Doctrine

nationalSpirits.description: The massacre of the socialists and indigenous people in Western El Salvador has left scars on our nation, with socialist guerrilla traitors lying around every corner. Should the United States prove unable to intervene, it could lead to an outright collapse of our regime.
nationalSpirits.name: Memories of '32

nationalSpirits.description: The Great Depression in the United States largely devastated our coffee market, and instability consumed our nation throughout the '20s as a result. Through numerous banking reforms and natural dissipation over time, the depression has largely left El Salvador but still affects our nation in some places.
nationalSpirits.name: Remnants of the Depression

nationalSpirits.description: Britain has always devoted itself to having the greatest navy in Europe, nigh the world. From the destruction of the Spanish Armada to the battle of Trafalgar and recently the near war winning naval starvation of the Teutonic hordes of central Europe, control of the sea has always been the priority of our nations armed forces. Yet, while we have cast off many reactionary traditions our love of the navy has remained, we must always be at the forefront of naval research and development. We must always Rule the Waves.
nationalSpirits.name: Naval Devotion

nationalSpirits.description: The Baltic governorates were developed with Riga in mind. It is the main industrial centre and infrastructure hub of the region and the largest city in the Baltic states, and the industry in Livland, Courland and Estland is reliant on a stable connection with its services. Now, a border stands between Riga and the rest of the Baltic states, giving its government great leverage in keeping the two other states in line.
nationalSpirits.name: All Roads Lead to Riga

nationalSpirits.description: Most Estonians are still farmers, many of whom are still using antiquated equipment and farming techniques. In order to free up additional manpower and better feed our people, including being able to send greater exports abroad, we will need to begin addressing the issues with serious and comprehensive reforms.
nationalSpirits.name: The Agrarian Issue

nationalSpirits.description: Our debt has reached a critical level and is a crippling burden on the shoulders of the state. People have begun to call the independence of Ethiopia into question because of how much our debt has tied us down.
nationalSpirits.name: Crippling Debt

nationalSpirits.description: Positions held within our armed forces are determined by birth and all of the top positions are held by men who are of noble blood and, yet, of questionable competence.
nationalSpirits.name: Aristocratic Military

nationalSpirits.description: Slavery is an extremely widespread practice within Ethiopia. Despite efforts, which were mostly symbolic in nature, undertaken by former emperors following Menelik II, slavery and descendants of slaves continue to exist and, despite working hard, receive no pay for their efforts. This institution is both inefficient and a great source of shame for Ethiopia as the practice of slavery is seen as improper for any civilised nation.
nationalSpirits.name: Slavery

nationalSpirits.description: Ethiopia, unlike the powers of the modern era, does not possess a united and organised army. The 'army' of Ethiopia, in fact, belongs to individual lords, whose men are loyal to them and only them.
nationalSpirits.name: Army of Levies

nationalSpirits.description: The Turkic people of Xinjiang were barred from most administrative posts under Chinese rule, leaving very few skilled bureaucrats for the government of East Turkestan.
nationalSpirits.name: Amateur Bureaucrats

nationalSpirits.description: Sisu is the uniquely Finnish expression for the resilience of the nation's people. Finland has faced harsh odds and will do so again.
nationalSpirits.name: Sisu

nationalSpirits.description: The Finnish people have been witness to the rapid German influence that has proliferated throughout the nation ever since the establishment of the Kingdom of Finland in 1918 following the victory of the White Guard in the Civil War. This influence can be seen in the form of treaties, German companies in the private sector, German-made weaponry, and the king himself, who is of German descent. As a result, the Finnish people have slowly begun to resent the increasingly tightening grip the German juggernaut has had on the kingdom, resulting in dissent which threatens to boil over at any moment.
nationalSpirits.name: Mounting Dissent

nationalSpirits.description: Officially titled the Central European Economic Union, Mitteleuropa is a customs and economic union unifying Germany and its sphere of influence, established after the Weltkrieg. Member states of Mitteleuropa find the impact of this agreement mixed - while the economic connections with Germany are beneficial, the agreement is heavily weighted in German favour.
nationalSpirits.name: Member of Mitteleuropa

nationalSpirits.description: While Fengtian may contain the second largest industrial base in East Asia, its size conceals obsolete machinery, inefficient practices, and severe mismanagement. Only extensive reforms, backed by a great deal of investment, can overcome these challenges.
nationalSpirits.name: Backward Industry

nationalSpirits.description: The economic collapse that followed Fengtian's entry into the last ZhiFeng War severely damaged its fiscal base and financial credibility, leaving the government with few creditors, and private businesses with severely limited options. Few have the confidence to invest in Fengtian, either at home or abroad.
nationalSpirits.name: Investment Dearth

nationalSpirits.description: The Kwantung Army has been in Manchuria for decades, but their crucial role during Guo Songling's revolt in 1925 gave all the leverage they needed to move their headquarters to Shenyang, greatly increasing their influence over the government. Now they operate as a de facto military mission and occupational force, protecting the railroads, providing material aid, and giving 'advice'. Unfortunately, ignoring this advice can have dire consequences.
nationalSpirits.name: The Kwantung Army

nationalSpirits.description: Mantetsu's economic influence spreads across the country and throughout the Assembly - at times beneficial, at others merely benign, but always concerning. While the Fengtian Government is currently committed to resisting Japanese influence, this may not last forever.
nationalSpirits.name: Mantetsu Influence

nationalSpirits.description: Our government's national goals have always clashed with more localised regionalist messages, which hold greater appeal among the broadly apolitical majority than high-minded republican ideals. Although Zhang Zuolin once rode regionalist sentiment to his current position as ruler, it now threatens to derail his plans to again go south of the Great Wall, conquer Beijing, and reclaim all of China.
nationalSpirits.name: Regionalist Sentiment

nationalSpirits.description: Despite years of reform, we still suffer from significant morale and leadership issues. Perhaps these issues can be solved in time for our forces to move south of the great wall...
nationalSpirits.name: Army Shortcomings

nationalSpirits.description: Despite various claims, there has never really been a \"Chinese Army\". Instead, the military is decentralised, highly factional, and irregular - the armies of the various warlords and breakaway states having grown haphazardly and semi-independently over decades of conflict. Most significant forces are regional, oversized, poorly maintained, and distrustful of one another, if not outright hostile. Corruption is endemic. Where logistics exist, most are simple coolie or mule trains complemented by regular robbery of the surrounding countryside. Though a few units appear to meet western standards, the vast majority do not, and better resemble gangs of bandits and other criminals. Even in peacetime, mere word of an approaching army is often enough for local peasants to flee the oncoming wave of looting and abuse.

effects.label: Supply Combat Penalties on Core Territory

nationalSpirits.name: Warlord Era Inadequacies

nationalSpirits.description: Despite its claims to the contrary, the Fengtian Government is plagued by endemic corruption, infighting, and abuse of power. While this is nothing out of the ordinary for China, it impedes the proper functioning of government and limits support for the regime. Should any of the governing factions gain too much influence, disastrous consequences are sure to follow.
nationalSpirits.name: Divided Governance

nationalSpirits.description: We are the legacy of the Paris Commune, the first socialist state ever created and then brutally repressed by the Republican reactionaries. In 1920, the workers finally got their revenge and overthrew the military junta of the 'Party of Order'. We, sons and daughters of Communards must protect our state and our spirit, we will not be commanded by tyrants anymore!

effects.label: Compliance Growth Speed in our states occupied by the enemy
Resistance Target in our states occupied by the enemy

nationalSpirits.name: Communard Spirit

nationalSpirits.description: Officially titled the Central European Economic Union, Mitteleuropa is a customs and economic union unifying Germany and its sphere of influence, established after the Weltkrieg. Member states of Mitteleuropa find the impact of this agreement mixed - while the economic connections with Germany are beneficial, the agreement is heavily weighted in German favour.
nationalSpirits.name: Member of Mitteleuropa

nationalSpirits.description: The amount of manpower our land based arm can recruit is severely limited. Strict regulations regarding foreign nationals joining, and a general lack of willingness by the natives, stifles our attempt to build a larger force.
nationalSpirits.name: Colonial Question

nationalSpirits.description: Through the AOG, we have vital economic rights in [?GEA_AOG_CITIES_NUMBER] important Chinese coastal cities: - §[592.GEA_GetStateControllerAllyStatus][592.GetName] - §[802.GEA_GetStateControllerAllyStatus][802.GetName] - §[803.GEA_GetStateControllerAllyStatus][803.GetName] - §[1075.GEA_GetStateControllerAllyStatus][1075.GetName]
nationalSpirits.name: Ausfsichtsrat der Ostasiatischen Generalverwaltung

nationalSpirits.description: Following Georgia's independence, the government was forced to sign the Treaty of Poti with Germany that protected our independence but gave vast economic powers to German companies. With nationalism on the rise, calls to end the Treaty have skyrocketed, but some fear it would lead to the death of Georgia.
nationalSpirits.name: Treaty of Poti

nationalSpirits.description: Georgia isn't just home to Georgians, but also has Ossetians, Abkhazians, and various other minority groups that feud with the central government.
nationalSpirits.name: Minority Protests

nationalSpirits.description: Officially titled the Central European Economic Union, Mitteleuropa is a customs and economic union unifying Germany and its sphere of influence, established after the Weltkrieg. Member states of Mitteleuropa find the impact of this agreement mixed - while the economic connections with Germany are beneficial, the agreement is heavily weighted in German favour.
nationalSpirits.name: Member of Mitteleuropa

nationalSpirits.description: The March Reforms to the Bismarckian Constitution, approved in 1920 after the fall of the OHL regime, laid the groundwork for a new era of genuine constitutionalism in the German Empire. A postwar consensus soon developed under the so-called \"March Coalition\" of the liberal parties and Zentrum, which sought to retain the achievements of March, tactically cooperate with the left or the right to prevent either of them from gaining power, and finalise the glorious conclusion to Weltpolitik. Content with keeping the SPD and the DVLP away from the Chancellorship, Wilhelm II endorsed this consensus, approving their Chancellors and offering cooperative ones elsewhere.  This consensus has come to an end. Decline of the Liberale Volkspartei, the arrogant and toady attitude of Chancellor Herbert von Dirksen, and growth of Reichstag's \"Permanent Opposition\" have all contributed to its death. In mid 1935, the March Coalition dissolved, and the Chancellor now has almost no support in the Reichstag. Defying expectations, the SPD and DVLP refused to call for a vote of no confidence against the Chancellor, intending to leave him to rot in the skeletal throne until the elections to the Reichstag this April. The beginning of April will cause the death of March.
nationalSpirits.name: March Leads to April

nationalSpirits.description: On August 12th, 1919, the guns fell silent. The Weltkrieg was over, and Germany came out victorious after five grueling years of warfare. It has now been made certain in the minds of the German population that the Imperial German Army is unstoppable - France has been beaten twice and Russia has been thoroughly dismantled. Even this victory did not make the brilliant minds of the Deutsches Heer rest - new weapons and techniques of war such as armoured vehicles and combined arms have been adapted to the traditional doctrine of mobile warfare, and the Luftstreitkräfte was established as an independent air force after a pitched political brawl in 1927.  As invincible as the German army seems, however, it suffers as an institution. The laurels of victory hide lacking central coordination, dominance of the military by aristocrats, and vitriolic interservice rivalry. The Heer has become divided into cliques, each with their own way to resolve the crisis, while motivation to reform the military among the civilian government is at an all time low - but if Germany is to win the inevitable Second Weltkrieg, these problems must be resolved.
nationalSpirits.name: Victors of the Weltkrieg

nationalSpirits.description: The German Empire is at the top of the world. Its rivals and enemies from 20 years ago have fallen to revolution, surrendered their empires, or gone into steep decline. All of the roads of this new world lead to Berlin - the economic, cultural and political heart of Europe. Our mission is to defend this new world with all of our might - as our enemies are numerous.
nationalSpirits.name: Deutsches Weltreich

nationalSpirits.description: Years of speculative investment and the proliferation of high value German government bonds have created a massive bull market in the Berlin Stock Exchange. The Stock Index of the Imperial Statistical Office is reporting record spikes in stock market price, creating a volatile, yet highly profitable market. Money is flowing fast and is rapidly funnelled into savings, investments, or, generally, even greater speculation. The consensus is that the spike in stock price will either last forever, or for just long enough that everyone can get their money's worth.
nationalSpirits.name: Christmas Spike

nationalSpirits.description: Officially titled the Central European Economic Union, Mitteleuropa is a customs and economic union unifying Germany and its sphere of influence, established after the Weltkrieg. Member states of Mitteleuropa find the impact of this agreement mixed - while the economic connections with Germany are beneficial, the agreement is heavily weighted in German favour.
nationalSpirits.name: Member of Mitteleuropa

nationalSpirits.description: Though the Legation Cities do provide us with the benefits of free trade, much of our profit from China stems from our investments in the AOG. Both illicit and legal trade provide our nation with a healthy stipend.
nationalSpirits.name: Fruits of the Open Door

nationalSpirits.description: Thanks to our incredible war debts after the end of the disastrous Weltkrieg, King Constantine signed a deal allowing German investors unfettered access to the Greek economy. As a result, almost half of our industry is owned by foreign creditors and banks - none of whom have our best interests in mind.
nationalSpirits.name: German-Owned Industry

nationalSpirits.description: Thanks to our incredible war debts after the end of the disastrous Weltkrieg, King Constantine signed a deal allowing Austrian investors unfettered access to the Greek economy. As a result, almost half of our industry is owned by foreign creditors and banks - none of whom have our best interests in mind.
nationalSpirits.name: Austrian-Owned Industry

nationalSpirits.description: While the Greek monarchy was officially abolished in 1931 after a tumultuous decade of coups and counter-coups, there are still those within our nation who continue to abide by monarchist principles, and are a major source of unrest within our nation.
nationalSpirits.name: Memories of the King

nationalSpirits.description: The Greeks are a people accustomed to war, and nothing stirs them up quite as much as the thought of their hard-won independence being taken away once more.
nationalSpirits.name: Legacy of Alexander

nationalSpirits.description: The Monroe Doctrine enacted by the US has caused our nation to lack a significant military force or the ability to go to war with other American countries in general. While this ensures the safety of our country, it severely limits the idea of expansion.

effects.label: Justify war goal time on us

nationalSpirits.name: Monroe Doctrine

nationalSpirits.description: The Socialists within Guatemala have been protesting with Mexican funding ever since the Dockyard and Railroad strikes, resulting in the government being forced to compensate the Socialists with empty reforms and changes often.
nationalSpirits.name: Socialist Compensation

nationalSpirits.description: The United Fruit Company has held a tight grip on Guatemalan politics and economy ever since Cabrera's dictatorship in 1898. While Guatemala has seen significant economic development as a result, it causes the United Fruit Company to hold Guatemala's fate in the balance.
nationalSpirits.name: United Fruit Company

nationalSpirits.description: Illiteracy has deeply affected Guatemala. While at the start of Orellana's regime the illiteracy rate was at 96%, the number has dropped down to 75%, mainly due to the reforms initiated in the country. However, this is still a problem, and it will likely haunt us until severe reforms are made.
nationalSpirits.name: Illiteracy

nationalSpirits.description: Liangguang has never fully recovered from the political instability of the 1910s-1920s. A revolving door of governments took hold over Guangdong and Guangxi as warlords, revolutionaries, and others took turns seizing power from one another. The defeat of the Kuomintang's National Revolutionary government in Guangzhou by the Zhili backed by German support allowed for Old Guangxi Clique warlords to take power, but their externally aided rule has been shaky. Guangdong warlords have rallied around Guangzhou, with the diminished but not fully extinguished Federalist movement enduring. Meanwhile, Kuomintang and other revolutionary cells continue to operate across the two provinces, hoping one day to return to power.
nationalSpirits.name: Unfinished Business

nationalSpirits.description: Liangguang is after all two provinces and with such a unique region naturally comes the problems of regionalism due to Guangxi and Guangdong's regional, cultural, and linguistic differences that have pervaded into the military forces of the province. The Guangdong Army is divided into a multitude of regional cliques and has fallen obsolete in comparison with forces such as the Fengtian Clique in the North while the Guangxi forces have been compared to be nothing more than organised bandit clans. As long as these forces remain divided and inadequate, Guangdong's potential to bid for a chance at national relevancy are but merely a fool's dream.
nationalSpirits.name: Divided Regional Military

nationalSpirits.description: The primary agricultural developments of Guangxi province have not been for the benefit of the people, but for the creation of commodities and raw wealth accumulation, creating an economy entirely hinged on the ebbs and flows of its exports. Controlled by the local gentry through a web of powerful landowners, magistrates, and allied militias, unrest over rents and taxation has triggered conflicts for generations.  Despite how essential exports are, both Guangdong and Guangxi often lack sufficient roads (or at least sufficiently maintained ones) for bulk agricultural transportation. Liangguang, as part of a China saddled with unequal treaties, cannot control import duties. A lack of capital due to poverty, political corruption, and endemic banditry (and the need to hire soldiers to guard against it) has prevented the two provinces (especially the inland Guangxi) from exploiting arable land, water, and mineral resources.  Domestic instability up until 1932 and falling exports from the American Great Depression have continued to hamper rural economic development in the two provinces. It would seem little changes in Liangguang.
nationalSpirits.name: Cash Crop-Focused Agriculture

nationalSpirits.description: Whilst a shining city on the horizon situated on the Pearl River Delta, Guangdong and its beacon of Guangzhou are merely developing when compared to the rest of the world. Its economic power was built up by the so-called \"Canton System\" between 1757-1842, which funnelled all Chinese foreign exports into the city and created a series of monopolies held by local merchants known as the cohong. This allowed Guangzhou (also known as Canton) to become a major entrepôt and access to foreign capital and trade allowed for the growth of local artisans and factories. However, this growth has been uneven, mainly for the benefit of foreign powers and their local compradors - spurring unrest and economic instability.  Domestic instability and the American Great Depression have hit Liangguang hard, and it is unclear how much more damage it can take.
nationalSpirits.name: Liangguang's Developing Economy

nationalSpirits.description: By the turn of the 20th century, China's literacy rate reached a significant disparity with the rest of the world despite the formation and spread of modern education as a result of growing ties with the rest of the world. Irregardless, as a region, Guangdong finds itself as one of the most literate centers of China with some reports recording that the literacy rate in metropolitan areas might be close to 80-90%.  Nonetheless, rural areas in Liangguang such as Guangxi continue to struggle with widespread illiteracy and it will take some serious reforms in education in order to administer widespread provincial literacy.
nationalSpirits.name: Struggling Literacy

nationalSpirits.description: Despite various claims, there has never really been a \"Chinese Army\". Instead, the military is decentralised, highly factional, and irregular - the armies of the various warlords and breakaway states having grown haphazardly and semi-independently over decades of conflict. Most significant forces are regional, oversized, poorly maintained, and distrustful of one another, if not outright hostile. Corruption is endemic. Where logistics exist, most are simple coolie or mule trains complemented by regular robbery of the surrounding countryside. Though a few units appear to meet western standards, the vast majority do not, and better resemble gangs of bandits and other criminals. Even in peacetime, mere word of an approaching army is often enough for local peasants to flee the oncoming wave of looting and abuse.

effects.label: Supply Combat Penalties on Core Territory

nationalSpirits.name: Warlord Era Inadequacies

nationalSpirits.description: The Haitian government lies on a thread - the position of  hangs in the balance. Beset by opposing forces, one must solidify their grasp of the nation as soon as possible as the political situation in Haiti becomes increasingly unstable.
nationalSpirits.name: Precarious Governance

nationalSpirits.description: We can't deny the elephant in the room; much of Haiti remains brutally illiterate, with schools heavily underfunded and most children being sent off to work at a young age. Higher education is typically reserved for French-speaking Haitians, and few resources exist for the average Haitian - those who speak Creole. While Haiti lags behind the rest of the world already, if illiteracy is not resolved, Haiti will continue to fall behind the rest of her neighbours.
nationalSpirits.name: Crippling Illiteracy

nationalSpirits.description: Despite the American withdrawal from their occupation of our island, Haiti continues to find herself placed firmly in the American economic sphere. Split between German and American economic interests, our people find themselves continuously exploited, and unless something significant happens to either power, we will continue to be subject to their hold.
nationalSpirits.name: Foreign Political and Economic Control

nationalSpirits.description: Since the withdrawal of US troops, the Dominicans have begun to build up their forces on our border and grow even more aggressive in their actions. Despite our desire to hit back, Dominican bribes have neutered our army. We must clean up corruption and modernise our army at least a little bit to be able to defend our borders.
nationalSpirits.name: Dominican Border Clashes

nationalSpirits.description: The workers of the plantations have gone on strike, demanding greater rights for workers, as well as more radically the destruction of the Big Five and Land Reform for the workers of Hawaii.
nationalSpirits.name: The Great Hawaiian Strike

nationalSpirits.description: The Civil War on the mainland of America has thrown the territory of Hawaii into chaos. Order must be restored to the island one way or fashion so that stability and prosperity can begin again in our tropical paradise.
nationalSpirits.name: Political Chaos

nationalSpirits.description: The Bureau of Ordnance influences any ship designs made.  This spirit is available due to our amazing torpedoes.
nationalSpirits.name: Bureau of Ordnance

nationalSpirits.description: Contrary to the less developed interior, the great cities of Hejaz are home to a strong and well established urban elite who participate in the world economy. These individuals, often former members of the Ottoman bureaucracy, army and institutions, have opinions of their own and have grown accustomed to the ideas of democracy and republicanism which were widespread in the former Ottoman state.
nationalSpirits.name: Unruly Urban Nobility

nationalSpirits.description: Home to the Holy Cities of Mecca and Medina, it is the sworn duty of our Sharif to protect and guide the faithful on their pilgrimage, or Hajj, to the Hejaz. Accompanying this duty however there are also significant benefits as our economy flourishes due to its connection to the Hajj. Shipping, caravan and motor companies have set up shops in the port city of Jeddah whilst a pilgrim tax is raised on every Muslim coming to visit our sacred places.
nationalSpirits.name: Guardians of the Hajj

nationalSpirits.description: Even though we may have been opposed to the Turkish nature of their regime, we can not deny that the Ottoman Turks have left in their wake a fully functional and extensive bureaucratic machine, unrivalled elsewhere on the peninsula. As we merely took over their system during the war for independence, many of the high level functions are still held by Turks whilst almost the entire administration of the former vilayet retains the Turkish language for communication and registration.
nationalSpirits.name: Engrained Ottoman Civil Service

nationalSpirits.description: Even before the revolution and subsequent civil war, India was a nation filled with great poverty, with its largely agrarian population significantly more destitute than those in other nations under the British crown. Combined now with the devastation of the civil war, India finds itself shockingly backwards compared to many of its contemporaries.
nationalSpirits.name: Widespread Rural Poverty

nationalSpirits.description: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, commonly simply known as his honorific of \"Mahatma\", is potentially the most important man in not only the Indian National Congress, but India as a whole. His influence is felt and respected by all those in the Republic's politics, even by those who harbour malice towards him over his vital role in securing a ceasefire after the initial revolution. Even with his continued pacifism putting him further and further at odds with militarists in the INC, there are few who can doubt his role as a great unifying figurehead for the Indian people.
nationalSpirits.name: Influence of the Mahatma

nationalSpirits.description: Following years of the Indian conflict being frozen in an unsteady peace, the Bharatiya army has slowly decayed into a state of unpreparedness for if the war were to actually restart, leaving many in the high command pushing for its immediate reform.
nationalSpirits.name: Unprepared Army

nationalSpirits.description: Unlike other provinces, Hunan is unique in that it has a constitution. Promulgated by Zhao Hengti and twelve others on January 1st, 1922, the Provincial Constitution seeks to uphold the rights of every Hunanese person, be they man, woman, and child. It promises free elections in the province of Hunan, with an elected Provincial Council and an elected Governor. While Zhao holds Hunan's Democracy close to heart, his commitment to his ideals (and the often rowdy Assembly) means that political deadlock is common. The Constitution also has a clause detailing Hunan's \"Monroe Doctrine\", which states that no Hunanese troops shall march out of Hunan, and no other provinces' troops may march into Hunan.
nationalSpirits.name: Constitutional Legacy

nationalSpirits.description: To the south lies the Shining Star of the Pearl River Delta, Guangzhou. To the northeast, lies the amalgamation of three industrial cities, Wuhan, and to the west, the practical metropolis of the interior, Chongqing. Yet lying in the crossroads between all of them, are the modest industrial hubs of Changde and Changsha. Towering far above the vast swathes of agrarian tilled land that innumerates Hunan Province, the two cities contribute the largest fair to our industrial capacity. Yet neither have received any due attention, with investors preferring to take their money to greener pastures in neighbouring provinces. This leaves the Hunanese government with a somewhat dangerous situation, for the entire industrial sector hinges on the success of two under-financed urban centres.
nationalSpirits.name: Perilous Industrial Sector

nationalSpirits.description: Not unlike the rest of China's interior, Hunan is a largely agricultural economy with scarce urban cities. Numerous villages and farming communities are scattered all throughout, with even more workers tilling their fields. Upon further analysis, one of the most striking characteristics of Hunan's — and the nation's, as a whole — agricultural system is the nigh Feudalistic nightmare that it represents. Local Gentry and Landlords rule their village communities like monarchs and their fiefdoms, and overwhelmingly the populace is worse off for it. However landowner interests are largely something the Changsha government has had to oblige with, for they control the strings that pilot the Hunanese economy.
nationalSpirits.name: Intense Agricultural Imbalance

nationalSpirits.description: Within China, Hunan is one of the few places where intellectuals can gather and speak freely. While this has been a wonder for advancement in our province, harbouring this many intellectuals can be costly on our relatively poorer province
nationalSpirits.name: Intellectual Hub

nationalSpirits.description: The western part of Hunan, Xiangxi, is dominated by two warlords, Chen Quzhen and Tian Yingzhao. Nominal loyal to Zhao, they hold greater sympathies with Tang Xiangming. Either way they serve as a thorn in the Governor's side, and they must either be compromised with, brought in line, or the Diarchy must fall.
nationalSpirits.name: The Western Diarchy

nationalSpirits.description: Despite various claims, there has never really been a \"Chinese Army\". Instead, the military is decentralised, highly factional, and irregular - the armies of the various warlords and breakaway states having grown haphazardly and semi-independently over decades of conflict. Most significant forces are regional, oversized, poorly maintained, and distrustful of one another, if not outright hostile. Corruption is endemic. Where logistics exist, most are simple coolie or mule trains complemented by regular robbery of the surrounding countryside. Though a few units appear to meet western standards, the vast majority do not, and better resemble gangs of bandits and other criminals. Even in peacetime, mere word of an approaching army is often enough for local peasants to flee the oncoming wave of looting and abuse.

effects.label: Supply Combat Penalties on Core Territory

nationalSpirits.name: Warlord Era Inadequacies

nationalSpirits.description: The 'Ambtenarenverbod' or Civil Servant Ban, blocks government officials from joining any far-left groups or the Landwacht, in the hopes of halting the momentum of these undemocratic ideologies.
nationalSpirits.name: Ambtenarenverbod

nationalSpirits.description: Officially titled the Central European Economic Union, Mitteleuropa is a customs and economic union unifying Germany and its sphere of influence, established after the Weltkrieg. Member states of Mitteleuropa find the impact of this agreement mixed - while the economic connections with Germany are beneficial, the agreement is heavily weighted in German favour.
nationalSpirits.name: Member of Mitteleuropa

nationalSpirits.description: The Monroe Doctrine enacted by the US has caused our nation to lack a significant military force or the ability to go to war with other American countries in general. While this ensures the safety of our country, it severely limits the idea of expansion.

effects.label: Justify war goal time on us

nationalSpirits.name: Monroe Doctrine

nationalSpirits.description: Honduras is a 'peasant republic'; that is to say it is run by the council in the name of the peasantry, and its official name is the Peasants' and Workers' Republic of Honduras. In practice, however, this government is moribund and has ceased to represent the people.
nationalSpirits.name: Peasant Republic

nationalSpirits.description: The December Revolution took place in 1932, when peasants occupied the capital and a loose coalition of different groups took power as the \"Peasants' Council of Honduras\". Now the revolution is regarded by some as a failure, but by others as having not gone far enough...
nationalSpirits.name: December Revolution

nationalSpirits.description: For the last century, the Honduran military has existed in name only, in reality the main military force of the country has lied on militia loyal to the PLH, PNH and local caudillos.  The long period of relative peace and stability since the end of the 1924 Revolution allowed the militias loyal to the government to begin professionalisation efforts, but the economic hardships brought by the great depression and the political instability that plague the republic after the 1933 coup have massively slow down these efforts.
nationalSpirits.name: A Military in Name Only

nationalSpirits.description: Officially titled the Central European Economic Union, Mitteleuropa is a customs and economic union unifying Germany and its sphere of influence, established after the Weltkrieg. Member states of Mitteleuropa find the impact of this agreement mixed - while the economic connections with Germany are beneficial, the agreement is heavily weighted in German favour.
nationalSpirits.name: Member of Mitteleuropa

nationalSpirits.description: After the Weltkrieg ended in 1919, the governments of Iceland and Denmark met to discuss the creation of the nation of Iceland. After brief negotiations, it was agreed that Iceland would be recognised as a sovereign nation held under a personal union between Denmark and Iceland. In exchange, Denmark would hold control over Icelandic foreign affairs and be responsible for the defence of Iceland if they are attacked.
nationalSpirits.name: Danish-Icelandic Personal Union

nationalSpirits.description: The collapse of the British Empire in 1925, was devastating to the Icelandic economy. Britain, a long-standing economic partner was now under embargo from Mitteleuropa. While Icelandic fish exports would eventually find Mitteleuropean buyers, the damage had already been done and the Icelandic economy was in shambles with the loss of one of its most profitable trade partners.
nationalSpirits.name: Ailing Economy
